spans.s:
लिङ्ख् लिङ्ख् (= rt. लख्), cl. 1. P. लिङ्-
खति, &c., to go, move.

लिङ् लिङ्, a technical term in grammar for
the terminations of the Potential and Precative or
for these Moods themselves (the Precative being
usually distinguished by the fuller term लिङ् आशिषि or
आशिर्-लिङ्).
—लिङ्-अर्थ-वाद, अस्, m. ‘explanation of
the sense of Liṅ, ‘N. of a grammatical treatise.

लिङ्कवाराहतीर्थ लिङ्क-वाराह-तीर्थ, अम्,
n., N. of a Tīrtha.

लिङ्ग् लिङ्ग्, cl. 1. P. लिङ्गति, &c., to
go; cl. 10. P. लिङ्गयति, &c. (more
properly regarded as a Nom. fr. लिङ्ग, p. 867), to
change or inflect a noun according to its gender;
[]
to paint, variegate; [cf. probably Old Germ. hring,
hringjan; Angl. Sax. hring.]

लिङ्ग, अम्, n. (perhaps connected with rt. लग्),
a mark, sign, token, emblem, badge, anything which
distinguishes or defines, distinguishing or discrimi-
nating mark, characteristic mark, characteristic, sec-
tarian mark; a symptom, mark of disease; a false
badge, any badge or mark assumed with a view to
deceive; a spot, stain; a proof, evidence, means of
proof, proof from a sure sign or token; (in logic)
= व्याप्य, the predicate of a proposition or the
mark which characterizes the subject (as in the pro-
position ‘there is fire because there is smoke, and
fire has smoke, ‘smoke is the लिङ्ग), inference,
conclusion, reason, (काव्य-लिङ्ग, a particular figure
of speech in which the grounds of a statement are
explained after the statement has been made); the
sign of gender or sex, organ of generation; gender
(in grammar, cf. पुं-लिङ्ग); the male organ;
Śiva's genital organ or Śiva worshipped in the form
of a Phallus, (this is usually of stone or marble, and
set up in temples appropriated to Śiva; there were
formerly twelve principal Śiva-liṅgas in India, of
which two or three of the best known are Soma-nātha
in Gujarāt, Mahākāla at Ujjayinī, Viśveśvara at Be-
nares, &c.); the image of a god, an idol; the subtile
frame or body which is not destroyed by death, the
indestructible original of the gross or visible body
[cf. लिङ्ग-शरीर, सूक्ष्म-श्˚]; = प्रातिपदिक, a
nominal base, the crude form or base of a noun
(shortened by Vopa-deva into लि); (according to
some) Prakṛti or Pradhāna (i. e. the primary germ
out of which all phenomena are evolved in the
Sāṅkhya phil.); the effect or product (i. e. according
to others, that which is evolved out of a primary
cause, and becomes in its turn a producer, = व्यक्त
in the Sāṅkhya phil.); the order of the religious
student; N. of a Purāṇa, (see लिङ्ग-पुराण.)
—लिङ्ग-जा, f. a kind of plant (= लिङ्गिनी).
—लिङ्ग-
तस्, ind. from a mark or sign, according to marks,
&c.
—लिङ्गतो-भद्र, अम्, n. epithet of a parti-
cular magical circle.
—लिङ्ग-त्व, अम्, n. the state
of being a Liṅga or mark, &c.
—लिङ्ग-देह, अस्,
अम्, m. n. the subtile or primary body, see लिङ्ग-
शरीर.
—लिङ्ग-द्वादश-व्रत, अम्, n., N. of a
particular religious ceremony.
—लिङ्ग-धर, अस्,
आ, अम्, wearing marks, carrying distinctive signs,
(मिथ्या-लिङ्गधर, wearing false marks, a hypo-
crite; cf. सुहृल्-ल्˚.)
—लिङ्ग-धारण, अस्, ई, अम्,
wearing a badge; (अम्), n. the act of wearing a
badge or any characteristic mark, the wearing of
a Liṅga or Phallus.
—लिङ्ग-धारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, wear-
ing a badge, wearing the Liṅga of Śiva; (ई), m. =
लिङ्ग-वत्, q. v.; (इणी), f., N. of Dākṣāyaṇī in
Naimiṣa.
—लिङ्ग-नाश, अस्, m. loss of character-
istic marks; a particular disease of the eyes, (loss of
vision from cataract &c., considered to be a discolora-
tion of the pupil); loss of the penis.
—लिङ्ग-प-
रामर्श, अस्, m. the groping after or seeking for
a sign or token (in logic), the consideration of a sign
or characteristic (as that smokiness is a sign of fire).
—लिङ्ग-पीठ, अम्, n. the pedestal of a Liṅga.
—लिङ्ग-पुराण, अम्, n., N. of one of the eigh-
teen Purāṇas (in which Śiva, supposed to be present
in the Agni-liṅga or great fiery Liṅga, gives an
account of the creation &c. as well as of his own
incarnations in opposition to those of Viṣṇu).
—लिङ्ग-प्रतिष्ठा-विधि, इस्, m. rules for the
establishment of a Liṅga.
—लिङ्ग-माहात्म्य, अम्,
n. the majesty or pre-eminence of the Liṅga, N. of
a section of several Purāṇas.
—लिङ्ग-मूर्ति, इस्, इस्,
इ, having the form of the Phallus (said of Śiva).
—लिङ्ग-लेप, अस्, m., N. of a particular disease.
—लिङ्ग-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having marks, possessed
of signs or tokens; having various sexes or genders;
furnished with a Liṅga or wearing a small repre-
sentation of the Liṅga of Śiva round the neck or on
one arm (applied as an epithet to a particular Śaiva
sect, also called Jaṅgamas).
—लिङ्ग-वर्धन, अस्,
ई, अम्, causing erections of the male organ; (अस्),
m. Feronia Elephantum.
—लिङ्ग-वर्धिन्, ई, इनी,
[]
ई, causing erections; (इनी), f. Achyranthes Aspera.
—लिङ्ग-विपर्यय, अस्, m. change of gender.
—लिङ्ग-विशेष-विधि, इस्, m. rules for the different
genders, N. of a grammatical treatise ascribed to
Vara-ruci.
—लिङ्ग-वृत्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, making a live-
lihood by false appearance or assumed outward marks,
hypocritical; (इस्), m. a religious hypocrite, one who
assumes the dress &c. of an ascetic to gain a liveli-
hood.
—लिङ्ग-वेदी, f. the pedestal of a Liṅga.
—लिङ्ग-शरीर, अम्, n. the subtile body which
accompanies the grosser in all its transmigrations and
is not destroyed by death.
—लिङ्ग-शास्त्र, अम्, n.
a grammatical treatise on gender.
—लिङ्ग-सम्-
भूता, f., N. of a particular plant.
—लिङ्ग-स्थ, अस्,
m. a religious student.
—लिङ्ग-हनी, f. = मूर्वा.
—लिङ्गाग्र (˚ग-अग्˚), अस्, m. glans penis.
—लिङ्-
गानुशासन (˚ग-अन्˚), अम्, n. the doctrine or laws
of grammatical gender.
—लिङ्गार्चन (˚ग-अर्˚),
अम्, n. worship of the Liṅga or Phallus.
—लिङ्गार्-
चन-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra work.
—लिङ्-
गार्चा-प्रतिष्ठा-विधि (˚ग-अर्˚), इस्, m., N. of
a work.

लिङ्गन, अम्, n. = आ-लिङ्गन, embracing, an
embrace.

लिङ्गिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a mark or sign, wearing
a distinguishing mark; having the character of,
characterized by (at the end of a comp.); wearing
or bearing the insignia (of any office or character),
bearing false marks or signs, a hypocrite; only
having the appearance or acting the part of (at the
end of a comp.; cf. द्विज-ल्˚); having a right to
wear signs or badges, one whose external appearance
corresponds with his inner character; possessing or
furnished with a Liṅga; having a subtile body; (ई),
m. a Brāhman of a particular order, a religious
student, an ascetic; N. of Parameśvara (as the sus-
tainer of Liṅga or Pradhāna, cf. लिङ्ग, col. 1); a
worshipper of Śiva in the Phallic type; a hypocrite
or pretended devotee; = व्यापक, the subject of a
proposition, that which possesses a characteristic mark
(as in the proposition ‘there is fire because there is
smoke, and fire has smoke, ‘fire is the लिङ्गिन्); the
cause or source (i. e. that original substance into
which a Liṅga is resolved, see under लिङ्ग); an
elephant; (इनस्), m. pl., N. of a particular Śaiva
sect [cf. लिङ्ग-वत्]; (इनी), f. a particular plant.
—लिङ्गि-वेष, अस्, m. the dress or the insignia of
a religious student (the skin, staff, bowl, &c.), the
dress or appearance of a follower of Śiva.
लिङ्गालिका लिङ्गालिका, f. a kind of mouse.
